title: Giving AI a seat at the peer review table - Nature Biotechnology
gist: Drosatos and Tsirigos argue in Nature Biotechnology that peer review is strained by reviewer time scarcity and propose AI as a bounded, non-voting, secure, auditable 'Reviewer 4' rather than a replacement for scientists. Only the opening paragraphs are visible; the rest is paywalled.

insights.claim: External peer review is a foundational component of science and has anchored merit-based research since the eighteenth century, but time, the resource reviewers most need for a thorough and fair review, has become scarce.
insights.speaker: Konstantinos Drosatos and Aristotelis Tsirigos
insights.so_what: The bottleneck in scientific quality control is reviewer time, which is the point where automation is most tempting.
insights.quote: time, which is the most essential element that scientists need to complete a thorough and fair review, has become scarce
insights.locator: External peer review constitutes a foundational component

insights.claim: Reviewers must assess large volumes of complex data while also managing their own research and grants, clinical duties, teaching, mentoring and administration, so workloads have grown while the review process structure has stayed unchanged.
insights.speaker: Konstantinos Drosatos and Aristotelis Tsirigos
insights.so_what: Rising load on unpaid reviewers degrades review depth, creating demand for tooling.
insights.locator: A manuscript or grant application reviewer must evaluate

insights.claim: The basic structure of peer review is still three scientists evaluating a manuscript or grant application, with editorial boards and funding agencies deciding mainly on those experts' assessments.
insights.speaker: Konstantinos Drosatos and Aristotelis Tsirigos
insights.so_what: The three-reviewer template is the baseline any AI-augmented model would modify.
insights.quote: three scientists evaluate a manuscript or a grant application

insights.claim: AI has become a multipurpose research tool that can perform many tasks of peer reviewers, which creates an opportunity to refocus and strengthen peer review.
insights.speaker: Konstantinos Drosatos and Aristotelis Tsirigos
insights.so_what: Publishers and funders are a likely early institutional buyer of reviewer-assist AI.
insights.quote: it can perform many tasks of peer reviewers

insights.claim: The authors propose AI as a bounded, non-voting, secure, auditable tool serving as an additional 'Reviewer 4' rather than replacing scientists, a framework with four design constraints on AI in review.
insights.speaker: Konstantinos Drosatos and Aristotelis Tsirigos
insights.so_what: Non-voting and auditable constraints define what adoption would look like and what vendors must meet.
insights.quote: with AI as a bounded, non-voting, secure, auditable tool — not replacing scientists, but serving as an additional ‘Reviewer 4’

insights.claim: The piece is published in Nature Biotechnology on 26 October 2026 as a policy piece by authors from the University of Cincinnati and NYU Grossman School of Medicine, and the full text is behind a subscription paywall, so the detailed proposal is not visible.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Specifics of safeguards and evidence cannot be assessed from the preview.
insights.locator: This is a preview of subscription content
